NPDES Appeal No. 26-01M 

ORDER GRANTING EXTENSION OF TIME TO FILE BRIEF 

Decided January 6, 2026 

Order of the Board by Judge Avila: 
The Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority (“ABCWUA”) filed a 
“Notice of Appeal” and an attached motion seeking an extension of time to file its brief in the 
above-captioned matter to February 23, 2026. ABCWUA Motion for Extension of Time 1 
(Jan. 5, 2026). ABCWUA represents “the complexity of the permit conditions” and 
“mandated administrative closures and reduced staffing levels significantly constrain[ing] the 
* * * ability to conduct the necessary technical and legal evaluations” as grounds for the 
extension request. Id. ABCWUA also states that the extension will not result in prejudice to 
any party. Id. at 2. ABCWUA represents that New Mexico Environment Department, EPA 
Region 6, and the Pueblo of Isleta do not oppose the requested relief. Id. ABCWUA 
represents they attempted, but did not receive a response from Amigos Bravos and the New 
Mexico Acequia Association. Id.

Based on the representations in the motion, the Board GRANTS the requested 
extension of time. See 40 C.F.R. § 124.19(f)(6), (n). ABCWUA must file its brief on or 
before Monday, February 23, 2026. 
So ordered.

NPDES Appeal No. 26-01M 
ORDER CLARIFYING THE EFFECT OF 40 C.F.R. § 124.16 
January 23, 2026 
Before Environmental Appeals Judges Aaron P. Avila and Ammie Roseman-Orr. 
Per Curiam: 
The Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water Utility Authority (“ABCWUA”) filed a 
“Notice of Appeal” seeking review of a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System 
(“NPDES”) permit decision issued by U.S. EPA Region 6, and a motion requesting an extension 
of time to file its brief. Notice of Appeal (Jan. 5, 2026); Motion for Extension of Time (Jan. 5, 
2026). The Environmental Appeals Board granted the requested extension, allowing ABCWUA 
to file its brief on or before Monday, February 23, 2026. Order Granting Extension of Time to 
File Brief (Jan. 6, 2026). Noting that the above-referenced NPDES permit takes effect on 
February 1, 2026, ABCWUA has now filed a motion requesting that the Board stay the permit 
limitations for total dissolved solids. Motion to Stay Permit Limitations for Total Dissolved 
Solids, at 1 (Jan. 16, 2026) (“Mot.”). ABCWUA represents that it “sought the positions of the 
F I
L
E
D
Clerk, Environmental Appeals Board 
INITIALS ________________________ 
Jan 23, 2026

2 
interested parties * * * and received the following responses: EPA Region 6 opposes the relief 
requested because they understand the permit conditions were already stayed upon appeal, New 
Mexico Environment Department takes no position, and the Pueblo of Isleta does not object.” 
Id. at 2. It added that “[n]o other party provided a position.” Id. 
The relevant federal permitting regulations provide that “[i]f a request for review of a 
* * * NPDES permit under § 124.19 * * * is filed, the effect of the contested permit conditions
shall be stayed and shall not be subject to judicial review pending final agency action,” and 
uncontested conditions that are not severable from those contested are stayed together with the 
contested conditions. 40 C.F.R. § 124.16(a)(1), (2)(i). The regulations further provide that the 
Regional Administrator will notify the Board and the parties of any uncontested and severable 
conditions that will become fully effective and enforceable 30 days after the date of the 
notification. Id. § 124.16(a)(2)(ii). Thus, per regulation, ABCWUA’s request for review stayed 
the effect of all permit conditions. This is consistent with ABCWUA’s representation of the 
Region’s response with respect to the filing of this motion. Because the relief requested is 
already in effect, ABCWUA’s motion is DENIED. 
So ordered.

NPDES Appeal No. 26-01 

ORDER GRANTING UNOPPOSED MOTION FOR EXTENSION OF TIME 

Issued March 24, 2026 

Order of the Board by Judge Roseman-Orr: 

U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Region 6 has filed an unopposed motion 
requesting an extension of time until April 24, 2026, to file its response brief, the certified index 
to the administrative record and relevant portions of the administrative record in the above-
captioned matter. Unopposed Motion for Extension of Time, at 1 (Mar. 20, 2026). The Region 
represents, among other things, that the parties “are in active discussions over the possibility of 
resolving this appeal without the need for the filing of a response to the petition for review.” Id. 

Based on the Region’s representations in the motion, the Board hereby GRANTS the 
motion. See 40 C.F.R. § 124.19(n). The Region’s response brief, certified index to the 
administrative record, and any relevant portions of the administrative record are now due on or 
before Friday, April 24, 2026. 

So ordered.

NPDES Appeal No. 26-01 

ORDER DISMISSING PETITION FOR REVIEW AS MOOT 

Issued April 28, 2026 

Before Environmental Appeals Judges Aaron P. Avila and Ammie Roseman-Orr. 

Order of the Board by Judge Roseman-Orr: 

On April 23, 2026, U.S. EPA Region 6 notified the Environmental Appeals Board that it 
is withdrawing the above-captioned permit issued to Albuquerque Bernalillo County Water 
Utility Authority in its entirety, consistent with 40 C.F.R. § 124.19(j). In light of this 
withdrawal, the Board dismisses the petition for review in this matter as moot. 

So ordered.
